title: Graphical mess on newest AMD driver (25.8.1), on VULKAN, works on 25.6.1
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in a number of versions, exported games, etc. 

I'm not sure where it would introduce, to be honest. I tested a game made in 4.3 and it had the same issue, though. Repeatedly down- and upgrading graphics drivers is kind of messy.



### System information

Godot v4.5.beta (fc7624491) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Single-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21013.4013) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.90 GiB memory

### Issue description

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5394b8cd-2ca2-4380-a1b9-6b83453e236a

The graphics are an absolute mess. On OpenGL and DirectX12 everything is fine, but on Vulkan, it turns into this. 

You can see that the gizmos are okay, too if you look closely (viewer discretion is advised). The UI is also fine. I tried random Godot games that render in Vulkan, and had the same issue. 

Other Vulkan apps are fine as well. I tried multiple AAA and smaller games and other stuff that renders in Vulkan and have not encountered another issue so far. 

I think this issue might mean some sort of communication with AMD in case the issue is on their side for breaking Godot, but I have absolutely no idea how to go about that. 

The issue comes back as soon as I upgrade to said driver, and goes away when I downgrade. 

I'm hoping to see nobody being able to reproduce it (so it's just me!) because breaking an entire engine in a GPU driver does not bode well...

I will try older versions of Godot that have Vulkan to see if I maybe find a cut... Maybe this is fixable from here.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Update AMD driver (maybe reserved to RX 6000?) to 25.8.1
2. Watch Godot games in Vulkan and the editor look like above
3. Downgrade to the last recommended one, 25.6.1
4. Watch it work just fine.



### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

No need, does it everywhere. Keep in mind: Just putting a quad in the scene will only make it disappear. Only when there's a larger amount of stuff in it, it will actually actively detonate.
